name: data-file-viewer
description: Open and explore .duckdb, .parquet, .csv, .dta (Stata), .arrow/.arrows/.feather (Arrow IPC), .xlsx (Excel), .db/.sqlite (SQLite), and kdb+ data files right inside VS Code, without needing a separate database program. A sidebar lists every table in the file — click one to see its rows in a grid, or write your own SQL query to look at exactly the data you want. Click a column header to sort by it, or open the stats panel to see quick numbers for that column — minimum, maximum, average, and percentiles — worked out across the whole dataset, not just the rows on screen. For editable formats (.duckdb, .parquet, .csv, .arrow/.arrows/.feather, .xlsx, .db/.sqlite), double-click a cell to change its value and save it straight back to the file; turn on Safe Mode first to keep an automatic backup and see exactly which rows changed before you commit to the edit. Stata files open read-only; convert a copy with ETL when you need to edit the data. kdb+ tables are read directly in their real, original format — no conversion step — though they are view-only for now, since there is no way yet to write changes back into that format. Excel workbooks show each sheet exactly as the file holds it — every row and column, titles and footnotes where the workbook puts them — while every detected table gets independent filter, sort, statistics and plot controls directly on its own header cells. An edit rewrites just that one cell inside the workbook file, leaving the other sheets, the formulas and the cell formatting exactly as they were.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: Dataset parsing, SQL and editing require a trusted workspace.

dataFileViewer.diffRowThreshold.description: Above this many rows, automatic diff-against-backup highlighting is skipped after a query — use "Diff anyway" to run it on demand instead.

dataFileViewer.maxResultRows.description: Maximum number of rows a query result sends to the view. Every row of a result crosses into the view before the grid decides which 30 of them to draw, so an uncapped query over a very large table spends its time moving rows nobody looks at. The default of 50,000 keeps that bounded and the footer says when a result was capped. Set 0 for no cap. Sorting still runs across the whole result before the cap is applied, so the rows you see remain the true top N.

dataFileViewer.liveRefreshIntervalMs.description: Default Live refresh interval (milliseconds) used when a document has no auto-detected sheet_metadata poll-cadence hint. Also acts as a minimum spacing floor between live ticks.

dataFileViewer.previewFirstTableOnOpen.description: Preview the first table as soon as a file opens, instead of waiting for a click. For a file holding one table that click is pure ceremony; turn this off if opening a very large file should stay instant.

dataFileViewer.hotFilePatterns.markdownDescription: Filename patterns for the hot half of a hot/cold pair, with `{base}` standing for the cold file's name. Declarative because the writer's naming is not fixed: trading_project's `SQLITE_HOT_NAME` is `auto`, and a rename there would otherwise silently end live updates. Patterns are inverted to find the cold half when the hot one is opened.

dataFileViewer.numberLocale.markdownDescription: Decimal convention for CSV files. `auto` samples the file and decides; a file that carries no evidence is left as text and reported, rather than guessed at — reading `1.234` the wrong way is a silent factor of 1000. `en` reads `1,234.56`; `eu` reads Turkish/European `1.234,56`. Mirrors the ETL pipeline's NUMBER_LOCALE.

dataFileViewer.chartMaxPoints.description: Most points a chart will draw. A chart plots the rows your query returns, including its LIMIT, so going over this refuses to draw and reports the real count rather than plotting a prefix that would look like a complete series. Native charts support up to 200,000 points; larger values are refused.

dataFileViewer.debugLiveRefresh.description: Log Live refresh internals (stat-gate skips, watcher/timer triggers, backoff, auto-detect cache hits) to the "Data File Viewer: Live Refresh" output channel.

dataFileViewer.nullText.markdownDescription: Cell text read as "no value here" rather than as a word. A spreadsheet writes a gap as `=NA()` (cached as `#N/A`) or as the bare word `NA`, and read back those are strings sitting in a column of numbers — which types the whole column as text and drops it out of the chart's column picker without saying so. A column is converted only when every one of its other values is a number, so a column holding a real note keeps its text and the notice says which value decided it. Set to `[]` to read the file literally. The file on disk is never modified.

enumDescriptions: Split a sheet on blank rows AND blank columns, so two tables side by side are two tables.
Split on blank rows only — what the ETL pipeline does. Tables side by side stay fused into one wide table.
Offer the sheets alone, with no tables detected inside them.
dataFileViewer.sheetTables.markdownDescription:
Whether to look for tables **inside** each sheet, and how.

The sheet itself is always shown exactly as the file holds it — every row and column, columns named after their Excel letters, titles and footnotes where the workbook puts them. Nothing is cleaned, promoted or moved. This setting only decides where inline table controls appear.

A published workbook rarely holds one rectangle per sheet: a footnote at the top, a table of series definitions, then the data, and often two tables side by side. Each detected table gets its own filter, sort, statistics and plot controls with real column types, while the sheet stays untouched.

`grid` (the default) splits on blank rows and blank columns. `rows` splits on blank rows only, matching the ETL pipeline. `off` skips detection. The file is never modified in any of the three.
